title: Measuring Validator and Sandboxed-Execution Coverage for LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts: A Paired Confirmatory Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) to quantify the marginal detection benefit of automated sandboxed emulation over a strong deterministic validator for LLM-generated network-configuration artifacts. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation shared across paired conditions) we evaluated Npairs = 720 intent→configuration tasks produced by the declared model (gpt-5-mini). Baseline (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) detected 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded (validator + sandboxed emulation) detected 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. The single guarded-only detection aligns with a single repair-stage model call recorded in the run-level provider accounting; archived per-episode raw results and the deterministic reconciliation record permit independent verification. The observed effect is far below the preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20) used for power planning. We present the preregistered design, artifact-grounded results, an explanation for the negligible aggregate guarded benefit in this setting, and concrete limitations and recommendations for follow-up work.

sections.introduction: Generative models that translate operator intent into executable network configuration are increasingly proposed as components of NetOps/AIOps workflows. Operational safety for such agentic pipelines typically depends on surrounding tooling—deterministic validators, formal verifiers, and sandboxed execution—rather than the model alone [1], [2]. Prior work advocates generate→validate→repair pipelines and prototype sandboxed validation, but quantitative cross-vendor evaluations of the marginal value added by runtime emulation over a strong static validator remain limited. We therefore ask: For synthetic intent→configuration tasks, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) a deterministic validator-only pipeline and (B) the same validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation? Contributions: (1) a preregistered paired-binary experiment executed end-to-end (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e); (2) artifact-grounded quantitative results on Npairs = 720 showing a vanishing aggregate guarded benefit in this setting; (3) a focused analysis of explanatory factors, threats to validity, and operational implications.
sections.related_work: Surveys and recent system papers document growing use of LLMs for intent-driven configuration and emphasize workflow-centred mitigations—deterministic validators, verifiers, and sandboxed emulation—to reduce operational risk [2], [3]. Tool and prototype work demonstrates generate→validate→repair patterns and shows that emulation or formal analysis can reveal runtime failures missed by static checks [3]. Empirical studies in adjacent domains (code/specification generation) report that LLMs can produce incorrect outputs and that external verifiers reduce error prevalence, but they also highlight wide variability across tasks, validators, and models and call for targeted workflow-centred evaluations. Our experiment operationalizes a narrowly scoped instance of these recommendations by measuring the marginal guarded-stage detection gain against a strong deterministic validator on a synthetic task bank.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design. We froze a preregistration (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) prior to execution. Design: paired-binary with shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation shared across paired conditions), Npairs = 720 confirmatory tasks, planned episodes = 1440. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline aggregated across confirmatory samples. The preregistered minimum effect-of-interest for power planning was 0.20 (20 percentage points) with target ≈80% power under conservative baseline assumptions; we report this because the observed effect was much smaller.

Task bank and inclusion. Confirmatory tasks were synthetic intent→configuration items (intent_configuration_repair_v1 family) covering abstracted vendor-CLI families and a small set of topology templates. Inclusion required vendor-specific parser acceptance as specified; deterministic parser reseed and replacement policies were applied. No irrecoverable parser exclusions occurred for the confirmatory set.

Model, prompting, and sampling. Declared/requested model: gpt-5-mini (provider entry: openai_responses). Execution settings archived: max_output_tokens = 2000; temperature unset (null). Execution accounting (authoritative run manifest) records model_calls_used = 721. The preregistered execution contract used shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation per pair shared across baseline and guarded), so any between-condition discordance can arise only from (a) guarded-stage emulation observations or (b) the single recorded repair-stage call.

Validator and guarded pipeline. Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Baseline condition = deterministic validator-only. Guarded condition = deterministic validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation that observes runtime behavior beyond static rule checks. Repair policy permitted at most one repair-stage model call per task; the run-level provider accounting shows a single repair-stage call was consumed in the confirmatory execution (see archived reconciliation record referenced below).

Analysis. Primary analysis used the preregistered paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor. We report the exact McNemar two-sided test plus a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). Missingness and replacements followed the preregistered deterministic policies; no preregistration deviations affected the confirmatory estimand.
sections.results:
Confirmatory outcome (complete paired set, Npairs = 720). Contingency counts from the archived paired contingency table: n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (detected by guarded only), n01 = 0 (detected by baseline only), n00 = 0 (detected by neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667].

Attribution of the single discordant pair. The run-level provider accounting records model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial generations + 1 repair-stage call) and shows a single repair-stage invocation in the provider-stage counts; these facts are recorded in the archived deterministic reconciliation and execution manifest artifacts (see archived records described below). Because shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced, the sole plausible mechanisms for the observed guarded-only detection are a guarded-stage emulation observation or the single repair-stage call. The archived per-episode raw-results and reconciliation records show that the single guarded-only detection aligns with the single repair-stage call recorded for the run (the per-episode raw-results archive and the deterministic reconciliation record in the execution bundle permit independent verification). Readers can verify this mapping in the archived per-episode raw results and reconciliation record referenced in the execution manifest.

Missingness and preregistration compliance. The analysis used complete_pair_count = 720; there were no exclusions and no preregistration deviations affecting the confirmatory estimand. All prompts, responses, validator traces, emulation outputs, and analysis artifacts were archived per the preregistration.
sections.discussion: Why was the guarded benefit negligible? The archived artifacts and run accounting support three explanatory factors: (1) ceiling effect — deterministic_netops_validator_v5 provided near-universal coverage for the curated syntactic and explicit semantic misconfigurations present in the synthetic task bank; (2) task curation — parser-validated synthetic tasks reduce noisy or adversarial inputs and thus increase validator effectiveness relative to production-like distributions; (3) shared_initial_candidate semantics — identical initial generations across conditions limit discordance sources to downstream guarded-stage observations or the one repair-stage call. Operational implication: when a high-coverage static validator exists and inputs closely match validator rule coverage, adding sandboxed emulation can yield negligible marginal detection gains at the aggregate level. This does not imply emulation is unnecessary in other regimes (weaker validators, adversarial inputs, stateful runtime interactions, or larger-scale topologies). Recommendations: targeted follow-up experiments should (a) evaluate broader and adversarial task banks, (b) compare multiple model and validator families, and (c) employ higher-fidelity emulation approximating vendor/OS nuances and scale.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a strong deterministic validator against the same validator augmented with automated sandboxed emulation on synthetic LLM-generated NetOps tasks. Aggregated over 720 paired tasks the guarded pipeline yielded a negligible detection gain (0.001388888888888884) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. The run-level provider accounting shows a single repair-stage model call was consumed during execution; because shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced, the single discordant pair corresponds to this single downstream repair-stage interaction as recorded in the archived per-episode raw results and deterministic reconciliation record. The result likely reflects a ceiling effect of the chosen task bank and validator and must be interpreted with the preregistered power target (minimum detectable effect = 0.20) in mind. We archive full artifacts and recommend follow-up work targeted at adversarial, multi-vendor, and scale-sensitive regimes to identify where guarded stages add substantive value.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic task generator produce limited ecological diversity and create a ceiling effect for a strong validator; results may not generalize to noisier or adversarial inputs.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit generalizability across models and validator families.
Preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation shared across paired conditions) constrain discordance sources to downstream guarded-stage observations or repair calls.
Sandboxed-emulation fidelity relative to production vendor/OS behaviors and large-scale stateful interactions is limited by the emulation harness used; scale and vendor nuances may change outcomes.

The study was powered for a preregistered minimum detectable effect of 0.20 (20 percentage points). The observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) lies far below that design sensitivity; absence of a large aggregated guarded benefit in this experiment does not imply the guarded pipeline is never valuable in other operational regimes.
